source_text: Si igitur legas opus meum, desines mirari, cur ad verba tua, quae supra posueram, reverterim. Promiseram quippe me de scriptis tuis probaturum, quoniam tu inter impietatem quam biberas, et eius invidiam quam time s, pariter utrumque dixisses, et quod a Catholicis, et quod a Manichaeis asseri solet. Est itaque ibi talis ordo verborum admotus tuo capiti, quod nunc fronte sycophantae interpolatum fuisse mentitus es. Scio me magna pollicitum, id est, ut de adversarii sermonibus approbarem et eos, qui homines opus Dei negant, iure damnari, et istum ipsum, qui hoc confitetur, nihil aliud agere, quam ut peculium diaboli confirmet esse quidquid de nuptiarum fecunditate procedit. Hoc enim genere, patrocinii sui quoque legibus, Manichaeorum opinio destruetur. Verum id tota libri eius exordia publicarunt. Ait enim opus esse divinum homines, qui ex nuptiis, id est, ex maribus nascuntur et feminis; qua sententia omne quod erat acturus evertit, nobisque assentitur dicentibus esse impios, qui haec audeant denegare. Absoluta igitur iam una pars est: superest ut ostendam id eum, quod nuper impugnarat, astruere. Quibus dictis partem tui capitis retractavi, in qua dixeras: Eos, qui de tali commixtione nascuntur, dicimus trahere originale peccatum, eosque de parentibus qualibuscumque nascantur, non negamus adhuc esse sub diabolo, nisi renascantur in Christo, et per eius gratiam de potestate eruti tenebrarum, in regnum illius qui ex eadem sexus utriusque commixtione nasci noluit, transferantur [n117] . Cur ergo putes hinc te excusari posse ab errore Manichaeorum, quia ausus es sententiam, cum qua omnibus ingenii tui viribus luctabaris, inserere; cum hoc non patrocinium erroris tui, sed testimonium sit stultitiae singularis, qui putas Calliphontis more virtutem et vitia, iustitiam et iniquitatem oratione tua posse in foedera convenire? Quod autem ait Apostolus: Qui eruit nos de potestate tenebrarum, et transtulit in regnum Filii dilectionis suae [n118] ; lege quartum operis mei librum, et tunc tibi quid Magister Gentium senserit, innotescet.
pass_a_gloss: If therefore you read my work, you will cease to wonder why I returned to your words which I had placed above. I had promised indeed that I would prove from your writings that you, between the impiety which you had drunk and the ill-will of it which you fear, had said equally both, both what is accustomed to be asserted by Catholics and what by Manichaeans. There is therefore there such an order of words moved up to your head, which now with a sycophant's forehead you have lied was interpolated. I know I promised great things, that is, that from the adversary's speeches I would approve both that those who deny humans to be the work of God are rightly condemned, and that this very one, who confesses this, does nothing other than confirm that whatever proceeds from the fecundity of marriages is the peculium of the devil. For in this kind, by the laws also of its own patronage, the opinion of the Manichaeans will be destroyed. But the whole openings of his book published this. For he says that humans are a divine work, who are born from marriages, that is from males and females; by which sentence he overturns everything that he was about to act, and assents to us saying that they are impious who dare to deny these things. One part therefore is already absolved: it remains that I show him building up that which he had recently attacked. With which sayings I drew back the part of your head in which you had said: Those who are born from such a mingling, we say draw original sin, and we do not deny that they, from whatever parents they are born, are still under the devil, unless they are reborn in Christ, and through his grace plucked out from the power of darkness, are transferred into the kingdom of him who did not will to be born from the same mingling of each sex. Why therefore do you think you can be excused from here from the error of the Manichaeans, because you dared to insert a sentence with which you were wrestling with all the strengths of your talent; when this is not a patronage of your error, but a testimony of singular stupidity, you who think after the manner of Calliphon that virtue and vices, justice and iniquity can come together into treaties by your speech? But what the Apostle says: Who plucked us out from the power of darkness, and transferred us into the kingdom of the Son of his love; read the fourth book of my work, and then what the Teacher of the Nations sensed will become known to you.

pass_b_english: If you read my work, then, you will stop wondering why I returned to words of yours that I had quoted earlier. I had promised to prove from your writings that, caught between the impiety you had drunk in and the hatred it aroused that you feared, you had said both what catholics and what Manichaeans usually maintain. Here, then, is the sequence of words I placed next to your opening statement, which you now, with a false accuser's effrontery, have lied about my altering: “I know I have made a great promise: to prove from my opponent's words both that those who deny that human beings are God's work are rightly condemned, and that this man himself, who acknowledges them to be God's work, does nothing except establish that whatever comes from the fruitfulness of marriage is the devil's property. In this way the Manichaeans' opinion will be destroyed even by the principles of its own defense. But the whole opening of his book has made this plain. For he says that human beings born from marriage, that is, from males and females, are God's work. By this statement he overturns everything he was about to argue and agrees with us that those who dare to deny it are impious. One part is therefore already settled; it remains for me to show that he builds up what he had just attacked.” (John 3:3–5)

After saying this, I returned to the part of your opening statement where you had said: “We say that those born from such a union inherit original sin, and we do not deny that, whatever parents they are born from, they remain under the devil unless they are reborn in Christ (compare John 3:3–5) and, rescued through his grace from the power of darkness, are transferred into the kingdom of him who did not wish to be born from that same union of the two sexes” (Augustine, On Marriage and Concupiscence 1.1). Why, then, do you think you can be cleared of Manichaean error because you dared to insert a statement with which you were struggling with all the powers of your mind? This does not defend your error; it testifies to your extraordinary foolishness. You imagine, like Calliphon, that your speech can bring virtue and vice, justice and injustice, into an alliance. As for the apostle's words, “Who rescued us from the power of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of his beloved Son” (Colossians 1:13), read the fourth book of my work, and then you will learn what the Teacher of the Nations meant.
